extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, and potential applicants looking for information about Schmidt Sciences and its funding programs
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the philanthropic organization's purpose, programs, and stated objectives to inform researchers or applicants about funding priorities and major initiatives. Focuses on Schmidt Sciences' named fellowships, research funding areas, and announced projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI2050 fellowship objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The AI2050 academic fellowship asks scholars to imagine a future in which AI has benefited society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schmidt Sciences awards the AI2050 academic fellowship and the Schmidts committed $125 million to the AI2050 program over five years. (Original phrasing: 'Schmidt Sciences awards the AI2050 academic fellowship which asks scholars to imagine a future in which AI has benefited society.')

rubrics_metrics.name: AI science safety research funding focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund scientific research into safety problems in AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 2025 Schmidt Sciences announced a new $10 million venture to fund scientific research into safety problems in AI; the AI science safety program includes 27 projects. Awardees announced in February 2025 included work on AI risk mitigation technology and research exploring AI attacks (examples: Yoshua Bengio; Zico Kolter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for ocean biogeochemistry research (OBVI partnership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner with Schmidt Ocean Institute to support the Ocean Biogeochemistry Virtual Institute (OBVI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schmidt Sciences partners with Schmidt Ocean Institute to support OBVI. (Referenced coverage notes '$45 Million for Ocean Science' in Sea Technology.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding astronomical instrumentation and observatory projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor and announce funding for large astronomical projects and instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In January 2026 Schmidt Sciences announced four astronomical projects: a private space telescope, Lazuli (proposed launch 2028); the Argus Array (1,200 telescopes to mimic an 8 meter optical telescope); Deep Synoptic Array (1,600 radio dishes); and LFAST, an instrument for large aperture spectroscopy intended for biosignature search. (These are presented as Schmidt Sciences' announced investments/projects.)
